title: 13 Acres Built to Feel Endless: Suzhou’s 500-Year-Old Garden | China Travel Expert
description:
How do you make 13 acres feel like it never ends?

Suzhou’s classical gardens use a 1,000-year-old design idea called "borrowed scenery" (借景) — a framed window or doorway pulls a distant hill or pagoda into the view, so a walled garden feels boundless. The Humble Administrator’s Garden covers about 5.2 hectares (13 acres) and was laid out in 1513. Nine Suzhou gardens are UNESCO World Heritage.

🧭 Expert Tip: Get to the Humble Administrator’s Garden right at opening — empty courtyards are when the "endless" illusion actually works.
